title: Microsoft Teams: delegators can lock calls and enable a delegate join tone
summary: Hold: the delegate-permissions command omits required Boolean values and cannot be used as printed. Microsoft also documents a permission to join active calls, contrary to the briefing's statement that no join permission is shown. The feature description and rollout dates match Microsoft's supplied notice and roadmap.

claims.claim: A delegator authorises a delegate to make or receive calls on their behalf.
claims.quote: In the context of call delegation, a delegator is the user authorizing a delegate to make or receive calls on their behalf.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Delegators can lock an active call to prevent delegates from joining it.
claims.quote: Delegators can lock an ongoing call to prevent delegates from joining or resuming the call

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A locked call cannot be resumed from hold by a delegate.
claims.quote:
Delegators can lock an active call to prevent delegates from:

- Resuming a call that has been placed on hold.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Delegators can optionally enable a warning tone when a delegate joins an active call.
claims.quote: can optionally enable warning tones that notify participants when a delegate joins or resumes a call.

claims.claim: The optional warning tone also sounds when a delegate resumes a held call.
claims.quote:
When enabled, all call participants will hear an audible notification when a delegate:

- Joins an active call.
- Resumes a held call.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: All call participants hear an enabled warning tone, including participants outside the organisation.
claims.quote: When enabled, all call participants will hear an audible notification

claims.quote: Delegators can lock an active Teams call directly from the Calls experience

claims.claim: Delegates continue to see locked calls in their call history.
claims.quote: Delegates will continue to see locked calls in their call history.

claims.quote: Delegates will be unable to participate in locked calls until the delegator unlocks the call.

claims.quote: A new optional Warning Tone for Delegate Participation setting will be available.Screenshot 3: New call delegation settings allow users to enable an audible notification

claims.claim: The cited Learn delegation article does not yet describe the new lock or warning tone.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "Warning Tone for Delegate Participation"; Teams "lock" "delegator". Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-call-settings in full: neither new control is described.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new controls are user-opt-in: delegators choose when to lock calls and whether to enable the tone.
claims.quote: Delegators can lock and unlock ongoing calls and can enable or disable the warning tone notification setting for delegate participation.

claims.claim: The delegation policy toggle is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > Delegation for inbound and outbound calls.
claims.quote:
select Voice > Calling policies.
2. Choose the policy you would like to update or select Add to create a new policy.
3. Toggle Delegation for inbound and outbound calls on.
claims.fix: Include the policy-selection step in the front matter and rendered table: Voice > Calling policies > policy > Delegation for inbound and outbound calls.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy in MicrosoftTeams supports Identity and AllowDelegation to control delegation availability.
claims.quote:
[-Identity] <string>
[-AllowDelegation <boolean>]
Enables the user to configure delegation in the Microsoft Teams client

claims.claim: The general AllowDelegation calling policy setting is on by default.
claims.quote: You enable delegation by using the TeamsCallingPolicy AllowDelegation setting. You can use Teams admin center or Teams PowerShell. This setting is turned on by default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrators access user call delegation settings through Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Voice.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, go to Users > Manage users and select a licensed user.
6. On the user details page, go to the Voice tab.

claims.claim: Set-CsUserCallingDelegate -Identity <delegator> -Delegate <delegate> -MakeCalls -ReceiveCalls -ManageSettings changes delegate permissions as printed.
claims.quote:
[-MakeCalls <Boolean>]
[-ManageSettings <Boolean>]
[-ReceiveCalls <Boolean>]
Set-CsUserCallingDelegate -Identity user1@contoso.com -Delegate user2@contoso.com -MakeCalls $true
claims.fix: Supply Boolean arguments in both copies, for example Set-CsUserCallingDelegate -Identity <delegator> -Delegate <delegate> -MakeCalls $true -ReceiveCalls $true -ManageSettings $true, explaining that administrators choose each value. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csusercallingdelegate as the command reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not show join permissions among delegate permissions.
claims.quote:
-JoinActiveCalls
Specifies whether delegate is allowed to join active calls on behalf of the specified user.
-PickUpHeldCalls
Specifies whether delegate is allowed to pick up calls on behalf of the specified user.
claims.fix: Replace the note in both copies with: 'Existing control. Set-CsUserCallingDelegate also documents -JoinActiveCalls and -PickUpHeldCalls permissions; these govern delegate participation generally, not the new per-call lock or warning tone.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csusercallingdelegate.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific admin UI, calling policy parameter or API is documented to require the warning tone or enable, disable or force the new call lock.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams delegation "warning tone" "policy"; Teams "lock" "delegator"; Teams delegation lock call warning tone admin policy. Opened user-call-settings, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy, Set-CsUserCallingDelegate and Graph call delegation overview; none documents either new control.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams delegate call lock warning tone license pricing billing; Teams delegation lock call warning tone admin policy licensing meter. Opened teams-phone-licensing and user-call-settings; neither names a meter for the lock or warning tone.

claims.claim: Learn lists joining active calls as supported on Teams Desktop, Teams Web App (Edge) and Teams IP phone.
claims.quote:
| Capability | Teams Desktop | Teams Mac App | Teams Web App (Edge) | Teams mobile iOS/Android App | Teams IP phone |
| Join active calls | Yes | No | Yes | No | Yes |

claims.claim: Learn lists joining active calls as unsupported on the Teams Mac app and Teams mobile app.
claims.quote:
| Capability | Teams Desktop | Teams Mac App | Teams Web App (Edge) | Teams mobile iOS/Android App | Teams IP phone |
| Join active calls | Yes | No | Yes | No | Yes |

claims.claim: The calling policy enables users to configure delegation relationships, rather than governing the new lock or tone separately.
claims.quote:
You enable delegation by using the TeamsCallingPolicy AllowDelegation setting.
When enabled, the end user can configure their delegation relationships directly in Teams.

claims.claim: Get-CsUserCallingSettings can show a user's delegates and delegators for an inventory of delegation relationships.
claims.quote: Get-CsUserCallingSettings - shows call forwarding settings, delegates, and delegator information for a user.

claims.claim: Learn advises cleaning up delegation relationships in Teams admin center when turning delegation off for a user.
claims.quote: When you turn off delegation for a user, you also need to clean up delegation relationships for that user in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.

claims.claim: Learn recommends assigning delegates and delegators the same calling policy.
claims.quote: Therefore, it's recommended that delegates and delegators are assigned the same calling policy.

claims.claim: A delegate is bound to the settings in their own calling policy.
claims.quote: the delegate is bound to the settings configured in their calling policy and the permissions of the delegator's calling policy are not transferred to the delegate.

claims.claim: The existing make-calls, receive-calls and manage-settings permissions are assigned per delegator and delegate.
claims.quote: New-CsUserCallingDelegate -Identity user1@contoso.com -Delegate user2@contoso.com -MakeCalls $true -ReceiveCalls $true -ManageSettings $true

claims.claim: Locking calls and changing the tone setting are deliberate user actions, not autonomous actions.
claims.quote: Delegators can lock and unlock ongoing calls and can enable or disable the warning tone notification setting for delegate participation.
